newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ATALANTA HONOUR TRAGIC PISANI'S MEMORY WITH A WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ATALANTA HONOUR TRAGIC PISANI'S MEMORY WITH A WIN.

text.p: Little Atalanta moved to joint-third in Serie A after beating Vicenza 3-1 on an emotionally-charged afternoon in Bergamo on Sunday in a game overshadowed by last week's death of their 22-year-old striker Federico Pisani.
"Chicco" Pisani and his 20-year-old girlfriend Alessandra Midali died in a car crash near Milan in the early hours of last Wednesday morning.
On Sunday, all Italian Serie A players wore black armbands in memory of Pisani while talanta chose to remember him in perhaps the best way possible -- with a win.
When Paolo Foglio opened the scoring for Atalanta in the 58th minute, he and his team mates rushed to kiss Pisani's No.14 shirt, hanging behind the Vicenza goal.
"We went onto the pitch thinking about him and in a sense we had a twelth man playing for us. In the end that 'numerical superiority' told in our favour", said Atalanta midfielder Domenico Morfeo.
The inevitable attention created by Pisani's death distracted attention from the ongoing Atalanta success story.

Unbeaten since losing to Bologna on November 24, Atalanta have picked up 22 points out of a possible 30 from their last ten games and now lie joint third along with Bologna, Internazionale and Parma, nine points behind leaders Juventus and four points behind second placed Sampdoria.
Atalanta striker Filippo Inzaghi currently tops the Serie A goalscorers' chart with 15 goals, one more than Roma's Argentine Abel Balbo.

The Atalanta recipe for success relies on a traditional blend of home grown talent such as Foglio and Morfeo allied to imported experience in the shape of former AC Milan striker Gigi Lentini and ex-Partizan Belgrade defender Yugoslav Zoran Mirkovic.
Despite their current league standing, however, Atalanta remain convinced that their real longterm seasonal objective is still first division survival.
"Being third in the table changes nothing for us. We're still nine points away from being sure of staying up in Serie A", said Morfeo on Sunday.
Ironically, Sunday's victory was gained at the expense of Vicenza, for so long the major surprise of this season.
One time league leaders Vicenza have now dropped to eighth place and appear to have gone off the boil, a point acknowledged by their coach Francesco Guidolin.
"We're not the brilliant side of the early part of the season and we'd better get back to our best quickly," he said on Sunday.
As for Atalanta, their next game is an away fixture against Internazionale from nearby Milan, always a tough game dominated by local rivalry.
Matching strides with the biggest names in Italian and European soccer is no new experience for Atalanta.
Although the Bergamo club has never won the Italian title, it did run second to Milan midway through the 1992-93 season before fading to finish in eighth place.
During the 1988-88 season, while playing in the second division, Atalanta went all the way to the semi-finals of the European Cup Winners' Cup before being eliminated by Belgian side Mechelen.
